en: Arjuna said: Some devotees, always steady, worship you in this way; others worship the undying, unseen Absolute. Which of them knows yoga best?

first: मय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते ।
en: Krishna said: Those who fix their minds on me and worship me, always steady and full of the highest faith, I hold to be the most perfect in yoga.
But those who worship the undying, which cannot be described, is unseen, present everywhere, beyond thought, unchanging, unmoving and constant,
who hold all their senses in check, keep an even mind toward everything, and delight in the good of all beings, they too reach me.
The struggle is greater for those whose minds are set on the unseen, for the goal that is unseen is hard to reach for beings who have a body.

first: ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः ।
en: But those who give all their actions to me, hold me as their goal, and worship me with single-minded yoga, meditating on me,
for them, whose minds have entered into me, I soon become the one who lifts them out of the ocean of death and rebirth, Partha.

first: मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय ।
en: Fix your mind on me alone and let your understanding rest in me. Then you will surely live in me from now on; there is no doubt.

first: अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम् ।
en: If you cannot hold your mind steadily on me, then seek to reach me through the yoga of steady practice, Dhananjaya.
If you are not able to practise either, then make work for me your highest aim. Even by doing actions for my sake you will reach perfection.
If you cannot do even this, then take refuge in me, control yourself, and give up the fruits of all your actions.
Knowledge is better than practice; meditation is better than knowledge; giving up the fruits of action is better than meditation, and peace follows that giving up at once.

first: अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च ।
en: One who hates no being, who is friendly and kind, free from the sense of 'mine' and from ego, the same in pain and pleasure, and forgiving,
always content, steady in yoga, self-controlled, firm in resolve, with mind and understanding given to me: that devotee of mine is dear to me.
One who does not disturb the world and is not disturbed by the world, who is free from excitement, envy, fear and worry, is dear to me.
One who wants nothing, is pure and capable, stands apart, is free from distress, and has given up all selfish undertakings: that devotee of mine is dear to me.

first: यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ।
en: One who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor craves, and has let go of both good and bad outcomes, and is full of devotion, is dear to me.

first: समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः ।
en: One who is the same toward enemy and friend, in honour and dishonour, in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, and is free from attachment,
who takes blame and praise alike, is quiet, content with whatever comes, without a fixed home, steady in mind and full of devotion: that person is dear to me.
But those who follow this life-giving teaching of right living as I have given it, with faith, holding me as the highest, are very dear to me.
